subtopics.label: Studies confirm PFAS 'forever chemicals' in Great Lakes
subtopics.attitude: Concerned about widespread toxic chemical pollution
subtopics.summary: Discussions center on studies revealing the widespread presence of 'forever chemicals' (PFAS) in all Great Lakes [112470017383354999, 112558571478391596, 112462177380305572]. These toxic substances are found to be ubiquitous in the basin and are even raining down on the lakes [112470017383354999, 112462177380305572]. Airborne concentrations, particularly near urban centers, are notably high and contribute to chemicals being on the rise in Lake Michigan [112558571478391596].

key_quotes.quote: Toxic ‘forever chemicals’ ubiquitous in Great Lakes basin, study finds
key_quotes.note: This quote directly states the core finding about the widespread presence of these chemicals from the studies.

key_quotes.quote: 'Forever chemicals' found to rain down on all five Great Lakes
key_quotes.note: This highlights a specific and impactful mechanism of how these chemicals are entering the lakes, linking to airborne contamination.

key_quotes.quote: airborne concentrations of PFAS — per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances — are much higher near Chicago, Detroit
key_quotes.note: This details the source and distribution pattern of the chemicals, emphasizing urban pollution contributions.

subtopics.label: Campbell's Soup Admits River Waste Dumping
subtopics.attitude: Informational / Reporting corporate environmental law violations
subtopics.summary: Posts in this cluster report that Campbell's Soup Co. admitted to illegally dumping waste into various rivers, including the Ohio River [115225775739463523] and the Maumee River [115217123939357315]. The company violated environmental laws like the Clean Water Act, with reports indicating these infractions occurred numerous times, such as "5,400 times" [115323810385035515] or "400 times" [115217123939357315].
